## Summary

Wired up Japanese localization for `/login` and `/register` using Guren's existing `@guren/server` i18n subsystem (previously configured but unused beyond a single welcome string):

- **`src/app.ts`**: added `'ja'` to `i18n.supported` (English stays first, so it remains the fallback/default locale).
- **`lang/en/auth.json`** (new) / **`lang/ja/auth.json`** (new): the login/register copy, moved out of the page components into paired catalogs with identical key structure (`login.title`, `login.heading`, `login.subtitle`, `login.email`, `login.password`, `login.remember`, `login.submit`, `login.footer_question`, `login.footer_link`, and the equivalent `register.*` keys).
- **`lang/ja/messages.json`** (new): Japanese translation of the existing `welcome` key, preserving the `:name` placeholder.
- **`resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx`** / **`Register.tsx`**: replaced hardcoded English strings with `useTranslation()` from `@guren/inertia-client`, driven by each request's resolved locale.
- **`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts`** / **`RegisterController.ts`**: the `title` option passed to `this.inertia(...)` now uses `this.t(...)` so the pre-hydration document title is also locale-correct.
- Regenerated `.guren/translations.gen.ts` via `bunx guren codegen`.
- Added `tests/AuthLocale.test.ts`, exercising both pages across the `Accept-Language` cases from the spec (Japanese-preferring headers → Japanese strings; absent/English/English-outranking/unsupported-language headers → unchanged English), plus a check that both `welcome` keys exist with the `:name` placeholder intact.

`bunx guren check --i18n` confirms catalog parity (20/20 keys in both locales), `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (11 pass, 0 fail) both succeed, and `bun run build` completes cleanly.
